mainEntity.name: What is the statute of limitations for filing a dog bite lawsuit in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: In California, the general statute of limitations for filing a personal injury lawsuit, including those stemming from a dog bite, is two years from the date of the injury. This means you typically have two years from the day you were bitten to file a lawsuit in court. If you miss this deadline, you may lose your right to pursue compensation. It's crucial to consult with an attorney as soon as possible after an incident to ensure all deadlines are met and your legal rights are protected.
acceptedAnswer.description: In California, the statute of limitations for dog bite lawsuits is generally two years from the injury date. File within this timeframe to protect your right to compensation.
